# What every tool can do, and who must agree (generated by `python diya_catalog.py write`; do not edit by hand)

Written 2026-10-18 for the blueprint's DIYA-036, -037 and -038. The source is `diya_catalog.py`; `tests/test_catalog.py` fails if a tool, a kind of action or a flow exists that is not listed here, if a tier does not match how the tool works, or if a new part of the code starts making outbound writes without being named.

## The risk tiers

| Tier | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | reads: looks, changes nothing outside Diya's own records |
| 1 | reversible local write: changes Diya's own database where the person can see and undo it |
| 2 | reversible remote write: adds something private to the person's own account; proposed only, the owner approves each one |
| 3 | external-facing: reaches other people (send, invite, share). Not built |
| 4 | destructive or privileged: delete at scale, account settings, public sharing. Not built; denied by default |

## The rule that makes it a broker

A **tool** the model calls can read (tier 0) or change Diya's own records (tier 1). It cannot change anything at a service. A **proposal** is the only way the model can ask for a change at a service (tier 2 and up): it writes a pending card, the owner approves exactly what is shown, and only then does the code run it, once (`diya_actions.py`). The model has no tool whose parameters name an address, a header or a credential. What comes back from anywhere outside is data, never an instruction (`untrusted` below), and is read by a model with no tools whenever it is mail, a repository or notes.

## The kill switch

One press of **Pause Diya** on the Status page (or `POST /api/pause`) stops the three ways Diya acts on her own: an approved action is not run (and "Approve" is refused, leaving the action waiting), scheduled automations do not run, and she does not write first. Chat, reading, approving later and editing memory still work; reminders still fire, because they are the person's own alarms (`docs/PAUSE_DESIGN.md`).

## Every tool, proposal and flow

| Name | Type | Tier | What it does | Reaches | Undo | Approval | Output may hold other people's words | Needs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `list_files` | tool | 0 | lists files and folders inside the allowed folders | none | n/a | none | yes | - |
| `search_notes` | tool | 0 | searches the person's notes folder | none | n/a | none | yes | - |
| `get_weather` | tool | 0 | asks a weather service for the weather in a place | the allowed weather host | n/a | none | no | - |
| `web_search` | tool | 0 | searches the web for a question | the search service | n/a | none | yes | - |
| `add_reminder` | tool | 1 | saves a reminder in Diya's own database | none | the person ticks it off or deletes it on the Reminders page | none | no | - |
| `list_reminders` | tool | 0 | lists Diya's reminders | none | n/a | none | no | - |
| `add_task` | tool | 1 | adds a task to Diya's own to-do list | none | the person ticks it off on the Tasks page | none | no | - |
| `list_tasks` | tool | 0 | lists Diya's own tasks | none | n/a | none | no | - |
| `search_home_assistant` | tool | 0 | searches the states of the person's Home Assistant | the person's own Home Assistant address | n/a | none | yes | Home Assistant connected |
| `search_notion` | tool | 0 | searches the person's connected Notion | api.notion.com | n/a | none | yes | Notion connected |
| `list_todoist_tasks` | tool | 0 | lists open tasks in Todoist | api.todoist.com | n/a | none | yes | Todoist connected |
| `list_calendar_events` | tool | 0 | lists the next events on the person's Google Calendar | www.googleapis.com | n/a | none | yes | Google Calendar connected |
| `list_google_tasks` | tool | 0 | lists open Google Tasks | tasks.googleapis.com | n/a | none | yes | Google Tasks connected |
| `propose_todoist_task` | proposal | 2 | proposes a task in the person's Todoist Inbox | api.todoist.com (only when approved) | by hand in Todoist: Diya cannot remove it | owner approves each action | no | Todoist connected |
| `propose_calendar_event` | proposal | 2 | proposes an event, just for the person, on their Google Calendar | www.googleapis.com (only when approved) | by hand in Google Calendar: Diya cannot remove it | owner approves each action | no | Google Calendar (add events) connected |
| `propose_google_task` | proposal | 2 | proposes a task in the person's Google Tasks | tasks.googleapis.com (only when approved) | by hand in Google Tasks: Diya cannot remove it | owner approves each action | no | Google Tasks connected |
| `propose_drive_folder` | proposal | 2 | proposes a new folder at the top of the person's Google Drive | www.googleapis.com (only when approved) | by hand in Google Drive: Diya cannot remove it | owner approves each action | no | Google Drive and Docs connected |
| `propose_google_doc` | proposal | 2 | proposes a new Google Doc with at most a line of text | docs.googleapis.com (only when approved) | by hand in Google Drive: Diya cannot remove it | owner approves each action | no | Google Drive and Docs connected |
| `read_mail` | flow | 0 | looks through the person's Gmail when they ask; the answer is written by a model with no tools | gmail.googleapis.com | n/a | none | yes | Gmail connected |
| `mail_write_refused` | flow | 0 | answers a request to send, change or delete mail with the fact that access is read-only | none | n/a | none | no | - |
| `study_repo` | flow | 0 | reads a public GitHub repository the person names and shows the evidence | api.github.com, raw.githubusercontent.com | n/a | none | yes | - |
| `explain_memory` | flow | 0 | says where a remembered fact came from, from the memory's own record | none | n/a | none | no | - |

Tools of MCP servers the person added (`mcp_...`) are not listed one by one: each is read-only, approved by the person one at a time, and pinned (`docs/MCP_DESIGN.md`).

## The parts of the code that can send something out

| Module | Why it may |
|---|---|
| `diya_connector_tools.py` | Notion search is a POST that only reads; the Todoist task is created only inside todoist_add_task_execute, which diya_actions.run calls after the owner approves |
| `diya_google_calendar.py` | Google's own OAuth endpoints: the token exchange and refresh, and revoking the permission |
| `diya_google_write.py` | the approved Google writes: every request goes through _send, called only from the kinds' execute functions |
| `diya_push.py` | web push to the person's own subscribed devices |
| `diya_telegram.py` | the person's own Telegram bot |
| `diya_warm.py` | the local Ollama, to keep the chat model loaded |

## Not built (so nothing here can do it)

Sending, drafting, replying to or deleting mail; inviting anyone to an event; sharing a file; changing or deleting anything that already exists in a Google account; account settings. Each would be tier 3 or 4 and would need its own entry, its own approval wording and its own tests before it could exist (`docs/GOOGLE_WRITE_DESIGN.md`, "Next").
